title: Bound for a product Gaussian Hessian coefficient
statement:
Let $I$ be a finite index set, let $v\ge0$ be a real number with $v\ne0$, and let $c,z,a:I\to\mathbb R$. Suppose $a(i)\ge0$ and, for every $i\in I$, the Gaussian density with mean $c(i)$ and variance $v$, evaluated at $z(i)$, is at most $a(i)$, and
\[
\left|\left(\frac{(z(i)-c(i))^2}{v^2}-\frac1v\right)p_v(c(i),z(i))\right|\le a(i),
\]
where $p_v$ denotes that density. Then for every $i,j\in I$,
\[
\left|\left(\frac{(z(i)-c(i))(z(j)-c(j))}{v^2}-\begin{cases}1/v,&i=j,\\0,&i\ne j\end{cases}\right)\prod_{k\in I}p_v(c(k),z(k))\right|\le\left(1+\frac2v\right)\prod_{k
i I}a(k).
\]
hypotheses_covered: The Gaussian density at each coordinate is at most $a(i)$
The absolute second derivative coefficient at each coordinate is at most $a(i)$
replaced: Let $I$ be finite and $v\ge0$. Write $p_v(c,z)$ for the $N(c,v)$ density when $v>0$ and set $p_0(c,z)=0$; define $G_v(c,z)=\prod_{i\in I}p_v(c_i,z_i)$ and interpret division by zero as zero. Assume $c,z,a\in\mathbb R^I$, $a_i\ge0$, $p_v(c_i,z_i)\le a_i$, and $|((z_i-c_i)^2/v^2-1/v)p_v(c_i,z_i)|\le a_i$ for every $i\in I$. If $v>0$, then for every $i,j\in I$, $|((z_i-c_i)(z_j-c_j)/v^2-\delta_{ij}/v)G_v(c,z)|\le(1+2/v)\prod_k a_k$, where $\delta_{ij}$ is the Kronecker delta.
